children: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said on Wednesday the OPEC+ group of leading oil-producing countries is set to complete a review of its members' production capacities by the end of the year.
OPEC+, which comprises members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, ordered the review last year to help set 2027 output quotas.

The assessment of production capacity could be a contentious issue for a number of countries. The review comes only months after the United Arab Emirates left OPEC and OPEC+ in May to pump more oil after years of arguing that its quota did not reflect its investment in capacity.
Four people familiar with the matter said that Iraq was pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity.
OPEC+ holds a meeting on November 29 and is expected to decide on its 2027 output policy.
